name: Organise
tagline: The million-strong workers' network to anonymously chat to colleagues, let off steam, and campaign for better pay and conditions.
sdg_alignment: SDG 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth
SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: subscription revenue from small fraction of users
platform trust dependent on anonymity guarantees

news_articles.headline: Organise, a platform for worker rights, raises £570K seed funding led by Ada Ventures
Worker-led network Organise reaches 1.7 million workers in the UK

awards: FT and Sifted Pioneers of the Post-Pandemic World 2020

policy_outcomes.description: 100,000+ members influenced UK Employment Rights Bill, including banning zero-hours contracts
G4S night shift workers won equal pay (£2,017/year extra) after Organise petition campaign
Ted Baker CEO resigned following employee petition on Organise
Government agreed not to introduce welfare voucher scheme for sick/disabled following campaign

outcome_methodology: self-reported campaign wins; petition signature counts; media coverage tracking
documented_limitations: platform does not fact-check user-generated campaigns
relies on public pressure rather than legal enforcement
small fraction of users pay subscriptions
governance_model: private company (Organise Platform HQ Ltd); founder-led (Nat Whalley, Bex Hay)
curation_criteria: open platform — any worker can start a campaign; no editorial curation
contributor_governance: worker-led campaigns; Organise team provides tools but does not direct content
community_ownership: commercially owned; mission-aligned but not worker-owned
controversies: open platform means unverified employer grievances can be published without fact-checking
political_bias_allegations: broadly left-leaning focus on worker rights; no formal allegations found
